title: Local parameter criterion for a strict normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $H\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $H$ is a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] if and only if for every $x\in X$ there are a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] and $0\le r\le d$ such that the stalk of the ideal of $H$ is $(t_1\cdots t_r)$. The empty product is $1$, so the case $r=0$ describes a point off $H$ and includes the empty boundary. In particular this local equation condition implies that $H$ is reduced and effective Cartier and that its finitely many reduced irreducible components have regular scheme-theoretic intersections of the expected codimensions, as required by the boundary definition.

source.place: Tags 0BI9 (definition-strict-normal-crossings) and 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), including the proof from regular intersections to local parameter equations; compare ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed pp.118--119. Since X itself is regular, the off-divisor condition is automatic.

proof.text: Assume H is a boundary. Each component is regular of codimension one at its points. Apply the regular-local quotient-kernel parameter theorem and the initial-quotient dimension formula to see that its stalk ideal has one generator; off its support use the generator 1. At x filter the finite component list to those generators in the maximal ideal. Let J be their scheme-theoretic intersection. The sum-of-ideals formula identifies its stalk ideal with the list of these generators. This ideal is proper, so x has a preimage in J. Its regular local quotient has dimension dim(O_X,x) minus the list length by the boundary hypothesis. Lift a minimal generating list for that quotient maximal ideal. The chosen component generators followed by the lifts generate the ambient maximal ideal and their length equals its dimension, so form a regular parameter list. The coordinate-product formula identifies the product of its initial component generators with the intersection of their principal ideals. The omitted component ideals are unit ideals. The reduced-union formula and H radical identify this intersection with the stalk ideal of H. This argument includes an empty component list and points off H.

proof.text: Conversely assume the local equation condition. The coordinate-product algebra makes each ideal stalk radical and generated by a nonzerodivisor. The component-stalk quotient formula then makes every local ring of $H$ reduced. The definition of reducedness proves $H$ reduced, and nonzerodivisor spreading gives an effective Cartier ideal on an open cover.

proof.text: Use the component-stalk calculus for reduced $H$ to obtain finitely many distinct integral reduced components with reduced union $H$. At any point of a selected component intersection, the component/minimal-prime bijection and the coordinate-product minimal-prime formula assign distinct parameters to the selected components. The sum-of-stalk-ideals formula identifies its local ring with the quotient by those parameters. Coordinate-product algebra makes this quotient regular of dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}-|J|$. These intersections are locally Noetherian: on affine charts a quotient of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, since projecting finite generators of the inverse-image ideal generates every quotient ideal. The regular-scheme local-ring criterion proves regularity of every intersection, including single components. Empty intersections have no points to check; the empty subset gives $X$. All clauses of the boundary definition now hold, including the final assertion. The empty boundary and empty ambient scheme are included.
